title: Egypt's Mummified Cats Lived Hard Lives, Skulls Show
paragraphs: Ancient Egyptians loved cats, and they made mummies of many of them. Scientists wanted to know how these cats lived before they died.

A team from Belgium studied 131 cat skulls from a place in Egypt called Beni Hassan. Fourteen skulls showed injuries, and nineteen had small holes behind the eyes, which can be a sign of illness or poor food.
The researchers think the cats lived in very crowded places. This may have caused stress, fights and disease. But they only had skulls, so some of their ideas are guesses.

questions.q: Where did the team come from?
Why are some ideas only guesses?
questions.a: Because the scientists only had skulls.
